Sweep, nebo průraz? Rozhodne to, co přij: Sweep, or breakout? What comes next decides
Včera jsme si vyznačili místa, kde leží: Yesterday we marked the places where liquidity lies. Today, what happens when price gets there.
Cena úroveň skoro vždycky na chvíli pror: Price almost always breaks a level for a moment. The question is not whether it breaks it, but what it does right after.
Sweep je krátký výpad za úroveň a rychlý: A sweep is a short push beyond the level and a fast return. The stops are taken, nobody stays beyond the level and the market turns.
Průraz je výpad, po kterém cena za úrovn: A breakout is a push after which price stays beyond the level. Candles close beyond it, the next ones don't come back and the move continues.
Předem to poznat nejde. Proto se na pror: You cannot tell in advance. That is why you never enter right on the break. You wait for the candle to close and look at where it closed.
Zavřela zpátky uvnitř a další svíčka jde: Did it close back inside and the next candle goes the other way? It is a sweep. Did it close beyond the level and the following candles hold beyond it? It is a breakout.
Pomáhá i čas. Sweep, který přijde v kill: Time helps too. A sweep that comes in a killzone, followed right away by a strong move the other way, is easier to read than a slow crawl around the level in the middle of lunch.
NQ v noci udělal low na 21 010. V 9:41 n: NQ made an overnight low at 21 010. At 9:41 New York time price slides to 20 996, that is 14 points below the overnight low. But the candle closes at 21 018, back above the level, and the next two one-minute candles rise. That is a sweep: the stops below 21 010 were taken and price came back. If instead the candle had closed at 20 990 and the next ones followed it lower, it would be a breakout and the overnight low would become a ceiling.
Za úroveň cena vyjede skoro vždycky. Swe: Price almost always runs beyond the level. You recognise a sweep by the fast return and a close back inside, a breakout by price staying beyond the level. Decide only after the candle closes.
Kdy poznáš, jestli šlo o sweep, nebo o p: When do you know whether it was a sweep or a breakout?
V okamžiku, kdy cena úroveň prorazí: The moment price breaks the level
Až podle close svíčky a toho, co cena ud: Only from the candle close and what price does next
Podle barvy první svíčky v seanci: From the colour of the first candle of the session
Předem to nevíš. Rozhodne close a násled: You don't know in advance. The close and the following candles decide.
Svíčka propíchne včerejší low, ale zavře: A candle pokes through yesterday's low, but closes back above it and the next one rises. What is it?
Krátký výpad pod úroveň a návrat zpět je: A short push below the level and a return is a sweep: the stops were taken and the market turned.
Cena prorazí high, svíčky zavírají nad n: Price breaks a high, candles close above it and don't return to the high. What is it?
Cena za úrovní zůstala a pokračuje, takž: Price stayed beyond the level and continues, so it is a real breakout.
Kde likviditu hledat: čtyři místa, která: Where to look for liquidity: four places everyone sees
Včera jsme si řekli, co likvidita je. Dn: Yesterday we said what liquidity is. Today, where you find it on the chart before price gets there.
Platí jednoduché pravidlo: čím je úroveň: A simple rule applies: the more visible a level is, the more stops lie at it. Where everyone looks, everyone hides a stop.
První místo je high a low předchozího dn: The first place is the previous day's high and low. They are called PDH and PDL. Every trader in the world sees them, which makes them the strongest.
Druhé místo je high a low noční seance,: The second place is the high and low of the overnight session, that is the move before New York opens. In the morning they tend to be first in line.
Třetí místo jsou equal highs a equal low: The third place is equal highs and equal lows: two or more highs or lows at almost the same price. They look like a solid ceiling or floor, and that is exactly why stops build up beyond them.
Čtvrté místo jsou starší výrazné vrcholy: The fourth place is older significant highs and lows, for example from last week. The longer a level holds, the more orders wait at it.
Před seancí si těchhle pár úrovní vyznač: Mark these few levels before the session. You get a map of places price may head for, and at the same time a list of places not to put your stop.
Je 8:00 newyorského času a NQ stojí na 2: It is 8:00 New York time and NQ stands at 21 050. Yesterday's high is 21 120, the overnight high 21 095 and the overnight low 21 010. Around 20 980 there are three lows close together, that is equal lows. The map is done: above price liquidity lies at 21 095 and 21 120, below price at 21 010 and 20 980. When price slides below 21 010 after the open, just pokes through it and comes back, you know it took the overnight low. And you also know the next target above is 21 095.
Nejvíc stopů leží u high a low včerejška: Most stops lie at yesterday's high and low, the overnight session's, at equal highs and lows and at old significant extremes. Mark them before the session.
U které úrovně čekáš nejvíc stop-lossů?: At which level do you expect the most stop-losses?
U náhodné ceny uprostřed dne: At a random price in the middle of the day
U ceny, kde se nikdy nic nestalo: At a price where nothing ever happened
High předchozího dne vidí každý, proto u: Everyone sees the previous day's high, which is why the most stops lie at it.
Dvě nebo víc den skoro ve stejné ceně: Two or more lows at almost the same price
Low, které je přesně v polovině dne: A low that is exactly in the middle of the day
Dvě svíčky se stejným close: Two candles with the same close
Dna těsně u sebe vypadají jako podlaha a: Lows close together look like a floor and buyers' stops build up below them.
Proč si úrovně vyznačit před seancí?: Why mark the levels before the session?
Abys věděl, kam cena může zamířit a kam: So you know where price may head and where not to put a stop
Mapa likvidity ukazuje pravděpodobné cíl: The liquidity map shows price's likely targets and the places where a stop is most at risk.
Co je likvidita: kde čekají cizí příkazy: What is liquidity: where other people's orders wait
Začíná čtvrtý týden a s ním nejdůležitěj: Week four begins and with it the most important word in all of ICT: liquidity.
Každý, kdo je v obchodu, má někde stop-l: Everyone who is in a trade has a stop-loss somewhere. Whoever bought has it below some low. Whoever sold has it above some high.
Stop-loss kupujícího je příkaz k prodeji: A buyer's stop-loss is a sell order. A seller's stop-loss is a buy order. So in places where many people have a stop, a pile of orders is waiting.
Téhle hromadě se říká likvidita. Nad vrc: That pile is called liquidity. Above highs lies buy-side liquidity, that is buy orders. Below lows lies sell-side liquidity, that is sell orders.
Proč to velké hráče zajímá: kdo chce kou: Why big players care: whoever wants to buy many contracts needs someone to sell them. Below a low they find a lot of sell orders at once. That is why price often heads exactly where the most orders are.
Pro tebe z toho plynou dvě věci. Likvidi: Two things follow for you. Liquidity shows where price will most likely go. And your own stop in an obvious place is part of that pile.
NQ udělal během dopoledne tři dna těsně: During the morning NQ made three lows close together around 21 000. Buyers have stops just below them, say at 20 995. That is sell-side liquidity. Price slides to 20 992, the stops trigger as sells, a big player buys against them and price turns up. Whoever had a stop right below the lows is out just before the move they were waiting for.
Likvidita jsou čekající příkazy, hlavně: Liquidity is pending orders, mainly other people's stop-losses. Above highs it is buy-side, below lows sell-side. Price often heads for them.
Uprostřed pásma: In the middle of the band
Pod dny mají stop-lossy kupující. Jejich: Buyers have their stop-losses below lows. Their stops are sell orders.
Čím je stop-loss člověka, který je v sho: What is the stop-loss of someone who is short?
Short se zavírá nákupem, takže jeho stop: A short is closed by buying, so its stop is a pending buy order above a high.
Proč cena často míří k likviditě?: Why does price often head for liquidity?
Protože velký hráč tam najde dost protis: Because a big player finds enough counterparties for their trade there
Kdo potřebuje koupit hodně, hledá místo,: Whoever needs to buy a lot looks for a place where many people sell at once.
Struktura na více timeframech: velký gra: Structure on multiple timeframes: the big chart commands, the small one times
Otevřeš hodinový graf a vidíš trend naho: You open the hourly chart and see an uptrend. You switch to the five-minute and price is falling. Which one is right? Both. Each just shows a different distance.
Pokles na pětiminutovém grafu je často j: A drop on the five-minute chart is often just a correction inside the hourly trend. On the hourly chart it looks like one or two smaller red candles within a rally.
Proto platí pořadí: směr určuje vyšší ti: Hence the order: the higher timeframe sets the direction, the lower one is for timing. The higher timeframe is called HTF, the lower LTF.
V praxi to znamená tři kroky. Na hodinov: In practice that means three steps. On the hourly chart you find out where the market is heading. You wait for a correction against that direction. Then on the five-minute chart you look for the moment the correction ends, that is a break back in the direction of the hourly trend.
Největší chyba začátečníků je opačný pos: The biggest beginner mistake is the opposite: they see a strong move on the one-minute chart and jump in without knowing they are going against the hourly trend.
Když si grafy odporují tak, že nevíš, co: When the charts contradict each other so that you can't tell what is trend and what is correction, the right answer is not to trade. That happens often and it is not a failure.
Hodinový NQ dělá vyšší vrcholy a vyšší d: The hourly NQ makes higher highs and higher lows, the last low is at 21 000. On the five-minute chart price falls from 21 120 to 21 050 and makes lower highs. Whoever sees only the five-minute chart wants to sell. Whoever knows the hourly knows it is a correction above 21 000 and waits for the five-minute chart to turn up. Only then do they look for a buy.
Směr ber z vyššího timeframu, vstup z ni: Take the direction from the higher timeframe, the entry from the lower. A move against the higher trend is most often a correction. When you are not sure, don't trade.
The hourly chart is rising, the five-minute is falling. What is it most often?
Konec hodinového trendu: The end of the hourly trend
Korekce uvnitř hodinového trendu: A correction inside the hourly trend
Menší graf ukazuje detail. Pokles na něm: The smaller chart shows detail. A drop on it tends to be just a correction of a larger rally.
K čemu slouží nižší timeframe?: What is the lower timeframe for?
Směr dává vyšší timeframe. Nižší ukáže,: The higher timeframe gives the direction. The lower shows when the correction ends.
The charts contradict each other and you don't know what the trend is. What do you do?
Vstoupím podle minutového grafu: I enter by the one-minute chart
Otevřu long i short: I open a long and a short
Without a clear direction there is no reason to trade. A day without a trade is not a loss.
Silný a slabý zlom: ne každý průraz znam: Strong and weak break: not every break means the same
Už víš, co je BOS a MSS. Oba jsou zavřen: You already know what a BOS and an MSS are. Both are a candle body close beyond an important level. Today you look at what that break looks like.
Silný zlom proběhne rychle. Jedna až tři: A strong break happens fast. One to three large candles with full bodies and small wicks go through the level and keep going. Price doesn't return to the level right away.
Slabý zlom je pomalý. Malé svíčky se k ú: A weak break is slow. Small candles crawl up to the level, barely cross it, have long wicks and alternate colours. Price often comes back soon.
Proč na tom záleží: silný zlom ukazuje,: Why it matters: a strong break shows that one side really wanted to trade and had the strength. A weak break shows rather that the other side eased off for a moment.
Tomu rychlému silnému pohybu se říká dis: That fast strong move is called displacement. You will cover it in detail in week five. For now it is enough to ask two questions at every break: how large were the candles compared with the surrounding ones, and did price stay beyond the level?
Pozor na opačnou chybu. Ani silný zlom n: Beware of the opposite mistake. Even a strong break is not a certainty. It is just stronger evidence than a weak one.
NQ má poslední swing high na 21 150. Var: NQ has its last swing high at 21 150. Variant A: three small candles approach it, the fourth closes at 21 152 and the very next one falls back below 21 150. That is a weak break. Variant B: one candle bursts from 21 138 and closes at 21 171, the next continues to 21 185. That is a strong break, buyers steamrolled the level.
Silný zlom je rychlý, s velkými těly a c: A strong break is fast, with large bodies, and price stays beyond the level. A weak one is slow, with wicks, and price comes back. Trust the strong one more, but it is not a certainty.
Jak vypadá silný zlom úrovně?: What does a strong break of a level look like?
Velké svíčky s plnými těly, cena jde dál: Large candles with full bodies, price keeps going
Rychlý pohyb s velkými těly ukazuje, že: A fast move with large bodies shows that one side had real strength.
Cena úroveň těsně překročí a hned se vrá: Price barely crosses the level and comes right back. What is it?
Pomalé překročení s rychlým návratem je: A slow crossing with a fast return is a weak break, often just a stop-loss grab.
Znamená silný zlom jistý pokračující poh: Does a strong break mean a certain continuing move?
Ne, je to jen silnější důkaz: No, it is just stronger evidence
V tradingu žádná jistota není. Silný zlo: There is no certainty in trading. A strong break just has more weight than a weak one.
MSS: první varování, že se trend láme: MSS: the first warning that the trend is breaking
Minule jsi poznal BOS, tedy zlom ve směr: Last time you met the BOS, a break in the trend's direction. The MSS is its opposite: a break against the trend.
MSS je zkratka z anglického market struc: MSS stands for market structure shift. In an uptrend it happens when price closes with its body below the last higher low. In a downtrend, when it closes above the last lower high.
Proč je to důležité: rostoucí trend stoj: Why it matters: a rising trend stands on higher lows. As long as they hold, buyers have the upper hand. When one of them falls, it is the first sign that strength is shifting to sellers.
Stejně jako u BOS se počítá jen zavření: Just as with the BOS, only a body close beyond the level counts. A wick below a low after which price comes back is a sweep, not an MSS.
MSS je varování, ne jistota. Trh se po n: An MSS is a warning, not a certainty. The market often still comes back after it and the original trend continues. It has more weight when it comes fast and with large candles, that is with displacement, and when a liquidity sweep on the other side preceded it.
V modelu z Tape je MSS třetí krok: nejdř: In the Tape model the MSS is the third step: first the sweep, then the MSS with displacement and only after it do you look for an entry.
NQ roste a poslední vyšší dno je na 21 0: NQ is rising and the last higher low is at 21 040. Price takes the high at 21 120 and turns. One five-minute candle slides to 21 035 but closes at 21 046. That is not an MSS, only a wick was below the low. The next large red candle closes at 21 022. Now it is an MSS: the body closed below 21 040, and fast. The uptrend got its first crack.
MSS je zavření těla za posledním swingem: An MSS is a body close beyond the last swing against the trend. A BOS confirms the trend, an MSS warns before its end. An MSS alone does not guarantee a reversal.
Co je MSS v trendu nahoru?: What is an MSS in an uptrend?
Zavření těla nad posledním vrcholem: A body close above the last high
Zavření těla pod posledním vyšším dnem: A body close below the last higher low
Knot pod posledním dnem: A wick below the last low
MSS je zlom proti trendu. V růstu tedy p: An MSS is a break against the trend. In a rally, then, the last higher low falls, and with a body close.
Čím se liší BOS a MSS?: How do a BOS and an MSS differ?
BOS jde ve směru trendu, MSS proti němu: A BOS goes with the trend, an MSS against it
BOS je na denním grafu, MSS na minutovém: A BOS is on the daily chart, an MSS on the one-minute
Ničím, je to totéž: They don't, it is the same thing
BOS trend potvrzuje. MSS je první zlom p: A BOS confirms the trend. An MSS is the first break against it.
Kdy má MSS větší váhu?: When does an MSS have more weight?
Když přijde pomalu malými svíčkami: When it comes slowly with small candles
Když přijde rychle a předcházel mu sweep: When it comes fast and a liquidity sweep preceded it
Rychlý zlom po vybrání likvidity ukazuje: A fast break after taking liquidity shows that the other side really took over the market.
BOS: důkaz, že trend pokračuje: BOS: proof that the trend continues
Z minulých lekcí víš, že rostoucí trend: From the previous lessons you know that a rising trend makes higher highs and higher lows. A BOS is the moment a new higher high forms.
BOS je zkratka z anglického break of str: BOS stands for break of structure. In an uptrend it means price broke the last swing high. In a downtrend it broke the last swing low.
Důležité je, jak ho prorazila. Počítá se: What matters is how it broke it. It only counts when a candle closes with its body beyond the level. When only a wick exceeds the level and the candle closes back below it, it is not a BOS.
Proč takové pravidlo: knot nad vrcholem: Why such a rule: a wick above a high often just takes stop-losses and price comes back. A body close shows that buyers really held price above the level.
K čemu BOS slouží: potvrzuje, že trend ž: What a BOS is for: it confirms that the trend is alive. After a BOS a correction usually comes, and that is where you look for an entry in the trend's direction.
BOS není pokyn k nákupu. Kdo kupuje hned: A BOS is not a signal to buy. Whoever buys right on the break buys at the end of the impulse, that is expensive. That was the previous lesson.
NQ roste a poslední swing high je na 21: NQ is rising and the last swing high is at 21 080. A five-minute candle runs to 21 090 but closes at 21 072. That is not a BOS, only a wick was above the level. The next candle closes at 21 095. Now it is a BOS: the body closed above 21 080. The uptrend is confirmed and you wait for a correction.
BOS je zavření těla svíčky za posledním: A BOS is a candle body close beyond the last swing in the trend's direction. A wick alone doesn't count. A BOS confirms the trend, it is not an entry signal.
Co je BOS v trendu nahoru?: What is a BOS in an uptrend?
Cena zavře tělem nad posledním swing hig: Price closes with its body above the last swing high
Cena zavře pod posledním dnem: Price closes below the last low
BOS je průraz posledního swingu ve směru: A BOS is a break of the last swing in the trend's direction, in a rally the last high.
Svíčka přesáhne poslední vrchol knotem a: A candle exceeds the last high with a wick and closes below it. Is it a BOS?
Ne, počítá se jen zavření těla za úrovní: No, only a body close beyond the level counts
Ano, když je svíčka zelená: Yes, when the candle is green
Knot často jen vybere stop-lossy. Rozhod: A wick often just takes stop-losses. Where the candle closed decides.
Co uděláš hned po BOS?: What do you do right after a BOS?
Počkám na korekci a hledám vstup v ní: I wait for a correction and look for an entry in it
Otevřu short proti trendu: I open a short against the trend
BOS potvrzuje trend. Lepší cena přichází: A BOS confirms the trend. A better price comes only in the correction.
Impuls a korekce: dva kroky vpřed, jeden: Impulse and correction: two steps forward, one back
Trend nikdy neběží rovně. Střídají se v: A trend never runs straight. Two kinds of movement alternate in it: impulse and correction.
An impulse is a fast move in the trend's direction. The candles are large, have full bodies and follow one another in the same direction. Price covers a lot of points in a short time.
Korekce je pomalejší návrat proti trendu: A correction is a slower return against the trend. The candles are smaller, overlap and alternate colours. Price gives back only part of what the impulse did.
V rostoucím trendu tedy vidíš: impuls na: So in a rising trend you see: an impulse up, a correction down, another impulse up. The low of the correction is the higher low from the lesson on trend.
Proč na tom záleží: kdo nakoupí na konci: Why it matters: whoever buys at the end of the impulse buys expensive and has to put the stop-loss far away. Whoever waits for the correction buys cheaper and has the stop closer. The same trade, less risk.
Pozor na jedno. Když je návrat stejně ry: Watch one thing. When the return is as fast and large as the impulse before it, it is not a correction. It may be the start of a turn and it is better to wait.
NQ vyrazí z 21 000 na 21 060 během čtyř: NQ bursts from 21 000 to 21 060 within four large green candles. That is an impulse, 60 points. Then eight small candles slowly return to 21 035. That is a correction, it gave back 25 points. Buying at 21 060 would mean buying at the top. Buying around 21 035 with a stop below 21 000 has a better price and a clear place for the stop.
Impuls je rychlý a jde s trendem, korekc: An impulse is fast and goes with the trend, a correction is slow and goes against it. You enter in the correction, not at the end of the impulse.
Podle čeho poznáš impuls?: How do you recognise an impulse?
Velké svíčky s plnými těly jdoucí jedním: Large candles with full bodies going in one direction
Impuls je rychlý pohyb: velká těla a mál: An impulse is a fast move: large bodies and little overlap.
Kdy je v rostoucím trendu lepší cena pro: When is the better price for a buy in a rising trend?
Na konci impulsu: At the end of the impulse
V korekci kupuješ levněji a stop-loss mů: In the correction you buy cheaper and can put the stop-loss closer.
Návrat proti trendu je stejně rychlý a v: A return against the trend is as fast and large as the impulse before it. What does it mean?
Může jít o otočení, počkej: It may be a turn, wait
Korekce bývá pomalejší a menší. Když nen: A correction tends to be slower and smaller. When it isn't, the trend may be ending.
Range: když trh jde do strany: Range: when the market moves sideways
Trh není pořád v trendu. Velkou část dne: The market is not always trending. For much of the day price just moves up and down between two boundaries and goes nowhere. That is called a range or consolidation.
Poznáš ho takhle: cena se aspoň dvakrát: You recognise it like this: price stops at least twice in the same band at the top and at least twice in the same band at the bottom. Highs are not getting higher and lows are not getting lower. The candles overlap.
Hranice ber jako pásmo, ne jako přesnou: Treat the boundaries as a band, not as an exact line. Price rarely turns on the same tick.
Uvnitř range je pro začátečníka nejtěžší: Inside a range is the hardest environment for a beginner. Breakouts often fail, price returns to the middle and stop-losses get hit on both sides. The middle of the range is the worst place to enter.
K čemu je tedy range dobrý? Nad jeho hor: So what is a range good for? Above its upper edge and below its lower edge stop-losses build up, that is liquidity. When the market breaks out of the range, it often takes one side first and then goes for the other. That will be the week on liquidity.
NQ se hodinu pohybuje mezi 21 040 a 21 0: NQ moves between 21 040 and 21 080 for an hour. It turned three times around 21 080 and twice around 21 040. That is a range 40 points wide. An entry at 21 060 in the middle has nowhere to go and no logical place for a stop. The right decision is to mark both edges and wait.
Range jsou aspoň dvě odmítnutí nahoře a: A range is at least two rejections at the top and two at the bottom without new highs or lows. You don't trade inside it; its edges are future liquidity.
Jak poznáš range?: How do you recognise a range?
Cena dělá vyšší vrcholy a vyšší dna: Price makes higher highs and higher lows
Cena se opakovaně otáčí ve stejném pásmu: Price repeatedly turns in the same band at the top and the bottom
Jedna velká svíčka prorazí high dne: One large candle breaks the day's high
Range jsou opakovaná odmítnutí na obou s: A range is repeated rejections on both sides without the highs and lows moving.
Kde je v range nejhorší místo pro vstup?: Where is the worst place to enter in a range?
Uprostřed nemá obchod kam jít a stop nem: In the middle the trade has nowhere to go and the stop has no logical place.
Co leží nad horní hranou range?: What lies above the upper edge of a range?
Jistý odpor, který nejde prorazit: Certain resistance that cannot be broken
Za hranami se hromadí stopy. Trh si pro: Stops build up beyond the edges. The market often goes for them before setting off the other way.
Minule jsme si vyznačili swing high a sw: Last time we marked the swing high and swing low. Now we read the direction from them. It is enough to compare each new high with the previous one and each new low with the previous one.
Trend nahoru: každý další vrchol je výš: Uptrend: each new high is higher than the previous one (higher high, HH) and each new low is higher too (higher low, HL). Buyers are willing to pay more and more and come back sooner on a drop.
Trend dolů je zrcadlo: každý další vrcho: A downtrend is the mirror: each new high is lower (lower high, LH) and each new low is lower (lower low, LL).
Platí obojí zároveň. Když jsou vrcholy v: Both must hold at once. When the highs are higher but a low falls below the previous one, the uptrend has its first crack. When highs and lows alternate without order, the market moves sideways and has no direction.
Směr čti na vyšším timeframu, než na kte: Read the direction on a higher timeframe than the one you want to enter on. On the one-minute chart structure changes every few minutes and mostly means nothing.
NQ na patnáctiminutovém grafu: dno 21 00: NQ on the fifteen-minute chart: low 21 000, high 21 060, low 21 030, high 21 090. The second low is higher than the first (HL) and the second high is higher than the first (HH). That is an uptrend. If the next low fell to 21 010, below 21 030, the trend would get a crack.
Trend nahoru jsou vyšší vrcholy a vyšší: An uptrend is higher highs and higher lows, a downtrend lower highs and lower lows. Both must hold.
Dno, které je výš než předchozí dno: A low that is higher than the previous low
Vrchol, který je níž než předchozí vrcho: A high that is lower than the previous high
Nejnižší cena dne: The lowest price of the day
Higher low je nové dno nad tím předchozí: A higher low is a new low above the previous one. It belongs to an uptrend.
Vrcholy jsou čím dál výš, ale poslední d: The highs keep getting higher, but the last low fell below the previous one. What does it mean?
Trend nahoru dostal první trhlinu: The uptrend got its first crack
Trend nahoru potřebuje vyšší vrcholy i v: An uptrend needs higher highs and higher lows. A lower low is a warning, not a finished reversal.
Na jakém grafu je lepší číst směr?: On which chart is it better to read the direction?
Na minutovém, je nejpřesnější: On the one-minute, it is the most precise
Na vyšším timeframu, než na kterém vstup: On a higher timeframe than the one you enter on
Vyšší timeframe ukazuje směr, nižší jen: The higher timeframe shows the direction, the lower only the timing.
Swing high a swing low: kostra grafu: Swing high and swing low: the skeleton of the chart
Cena nikdy nejde rovně. Jde kus nahoru,: Price never goes straight. It goes up a bit, comes back a little and continues. The places where it turns are called swings. A swing high is a top, a swing low a bottom.
Swing se dá poznat přesně a stačí k tomu: A swing can be identified precisely and three candles are enough. A swing high is a candle with candles on both sides that have a lower high. A swing low is, mirrored, a candle with candles on both sides that have a higher low.
Swing je potvrzený až ve chvíli, kdy zav: A swing is confirmed only when the candle on the right closes. While it is forming, price can still exceed the high. That is why swings are always marked on the chart with a one-candle delay.
Na swingech záleží ze dvou důvodů. Nad v: Swings matter for two reasons. Traders leave stop-losses above highs and below lows, so price often returns to them. And whether the highs and lows are rising or falling tells you the trend. That is the next lesson.
Swing na vyšším timeframu má větší váhu: A swing on a higher timeframe has more weight than one on a lower timeframe. One swing on the hourly chart hides dozens of small swings on the one-minute.
Na pětiminutovém grafu NQ mají tři svíčk: On a five-minute NQ chart three consecutive candles have highs of 21 040, 21 065 and 21 050. The middle candle has the highest high and both neighbours lower, so 21 065 is a swing high. A bit later three candles have lows of 20 990, 20 972 and 20 985. The middle low of 20 972 is a swing low. Between 20 972 and 21 065 there are 93 points and these are the two prices you mark on the chart.
Swing high je svíčka s nižším high po ob: A swing high is a candle with a lower high on both sides, a swing low a candle with a higher low on both sides. It is valid only after the candle on the right closes.
Tři svíčky po sobě mají high 21 040, 21: Three consecutive candles have highs of 21 040, 21 065 and 21 050. Where is the swing high?
Prostřední svíčka má high výš než obě so: The middle candle has a higher high than both neighbours.
Kdy je swing high potvrzený?: When is a swing high confirmed?
Jakmile cena udělá nové high: As soon as price makes a new high
Až zavře svíčka napravo s nižším high: Once the candle on the right closes with a lower high
Dokud svíčka napravo nezavřela, může cen: Until the candle on the right has closed, price can still exceed the high.
Proč se cena ke swingům často vrací?: Why does price often return to swings?
Nad vrcholy a pod dny leží stop-lossy: Stop-losses lie above highs and below lows
Swingy jsou vždy na kulatých cenách: Swings are always at round prices
Za swingy se hromadí příkazy. Říká se ji: Orders build up beyond swings. They are called liquidity and we will cover it in detail in week four.
Futures NQ a ES se obchodují skoro nepře: NQ and ES futures trade almost continuously. The exchange opens on Sunday at 18:00 New York time and closes on Friday at 17:00. Every day there is a one-hour break between 17:00 and 18:00. So a new trading day starts at 18:00.
Trh ale není celý den stejně živý. Den s: But the market is not equally lively all day. The day is divided into sessions by which part of the world is at work: first Asia, then London and finally New York. The borders between them are not official, different traders draw them a little differently. Tape uses this division in New York time: Asia 18:00–2:30, London 2:30–7:00, NY AM 7:00–12:00, lunch 12:00–13:00 and NY PM 13:00–16:00.
Pro NQ a ES je nejdůležitější 9:30 newyo: For NQ and ES the most important time is 9:30 New York time. That is when the US stock market opens, called the cash open, and it closes at 16:00. After 9:30 the chart tends to show the most movement and volume. In Central Europe it is usually 15:30, because New York is six hours behind. For a few weeks a year, when clocks change earlier elsewhere, the difference is only five hours.
Všemu, co se stane od 18:00 do 9:30, se: Everything that happens from 18:00 to 9:30 is called overnight trading. The highest and lowest prices from that time form the overnight high and overnight low. The Tape model marks these two levels in the morning and looks for a trade only between 9:30 and 11:00.
Všechny časy v ICT materiálech jsou v ne: All times in ICT materials are in New York time. So set the time zone in your chart to New York and you don't have to convert anything.
NQ se přes noc (18:00–9:30) pohybuje mez: Overnight (18:00–9:30) NQ moves between 20 960 and 21 080. The overnight low is 20 960, the overnight high 21 080 and the overnight range is 120 points. At 9:30 New York time, 15:30 in Prague, the cash session opens and during the first half-hour price makes another 90 points. In thirty minutes the market moved almost as much as during the whole night.
Hlavní pohyb na NQ a ES začíná v 9:30 ne: The main move on NQ and ES starts at 9:30 New York time (usually 15:30 in Central Europe). What came before, from 18:00, is overnight.
V kolik hodin newyorského času otevírá a: At what time New York time does the US stock market open (cash open)?
Akciová burza v New Yorku obchoduje od 9: The stock market in New York trades from 9:30 to 16:00. At 18:00 a new day begins on futures.
Nejvyšší cena předchozího dne: The highest price of the previous day
Nejvyšší cena mezi 18:00 a 9:30 newyorsk: The highest price between 18:00 and 9:30 New York time
První cena po otevření v 9:30: The first price after the 9:30 open
Overnight je noční obchodování před otev: Overnight is the night trading before the cash session opens; the overnight high is its highest price.
Overnight low je 20 960 a overnight high: The overnight low is 20 960 and the overnight high 21 080. How large is the overnight range?
Graf se skládá ze svíček. Každá svíčka s: A chart is made of candles. Each candle sums up one stretch of time with four prices: where price started (open), the highest it reached (high), the lowest it fell (low) and where it ended (close).
Tlustá část svíčky je tělo, vede od open: The thick part of the candle is the body, it runs from open to close. The thin lines above and below the body are wicks and show the high and the low. When the close ends above the open, the candle is rising. When below it, it is falling.
Timeframe říká, jak dlouhý úsek jedna sv: The timeframe says how long a stretch one candle covers. On a 1m chart it is one minute, on a 15m chart fifteen minutes. It is still the same market, just zoomed differently. Fifteen one-minute candles together make one fifteen-minute candle.
Model v Tape hledá vstupy na 1m grafu a: The Tape model looks for entries on the 1m chart and checks the direction on the 15m. The higher timeframe shows where the market is heading, the lower shows the exact place.
Minutová svíčka na NQ: open 21 000, high: A one-minute NQ candle: open 21 000, high 21 006, low 20 998, close 21 004. The body is 4 points, the upper wick 2 points, the lower wick 2 points and the candle is rising.
Svíčka = open, high, low, close za jeden: Candle = open, high, low, close for one stretch of time. The timeframe is the length of that stretch.
Co ukazuje horní knot svíčky?: What does a candle's upper wick show?
Nejvyšší cenu dosaženou během svíčky: The highest price reached during the candle
Knoty sahají k high a low, tělo vede od: The wicks reach to the high and the low, the body runs from open to close.
Svíčka má open 100 a close 97. Jaká je?: A candle has an open of 100 and a close of 97. What is it?
Close je pod open, cena během svíčky kle: The close is below the open, price fell during the candle.
Kolik 1m svíček tvoří jednu 15m svíčku?: How many 1m candles make one 15m candle?
15m svíčka pokrývá patnáct minut, tedy p: A 15m candle covers fifteen minutes, that is fifteen one-minute candles.
Co je NQ a ES a co znamená bod a tick: What NQ and ES are and what a point and a tick mean
NQ a ES jsou futures kontrakty na americ: NQ and ES are futures contracts on US stock indices. NQ tracks the Nasdaq 100, a hundred large technology companies. ES tracks the S&P 500, the five hundred largest US companies. You don't buy shares, you trade a contract whose price moves together with the index.
Cena se měří v bodech. Nejmenší krok, o: Price is measured in points. The smallest step price can move is called a tick. On both NQ and ES a tick is a quarter of a point, so four ticks make one point.
Each point has a fixed dollar value. On NQ it is 20 dollars per point, on ES 50 dollars per point. There are also ten times smaller contracts MNQ and MES, where a point is worth 2 and 5 dollars. Beginners learn on those, because a mistake costs a tenth.
NQ moves faster and by more points than ES. That is why in Tape the stop size is calculated in points for each market separately.
Cena NQ jde z 21 000,00 na 21 010,00. To: The NQ price goes from 21 000.00 to 21 010.00. That is 10 points, that is 40 ticks. On one NQ contract it is 200 dollars, on one MNQ 20 dollars.
Tick je nejmenší krok ceny, bod jsou čty: A tick is the smallest price step, a point is four ticks. Point value: NQ 20 USD, ES 50 USD, MNQ 2 USD, MES 5 USD.
Kolik ticků je jeden bod na NQ?: How many ticks is one point on NQ?
Tick je 0,25 bodu, takže bod jsou čtyři: A tick is 0.25 of a point, so a point is four ticks.
Cena ES stoupne o 3 body. Kolik je to na: The ES price rises by 3 points. How much is that on one ES contract?
Bod na ES má hodnotu 50 USD, tři body js: A point on ES is worth 50 USD, three points are 150 USD.
Proč se začátečník učí spíš na MNQ než n: Why does a beginner learn on MNQ rather than NQ?
Bod na MNQ má desetinovou hodnotu, takže: A point on MNQ is worth a tenth, so a mistake costs less
MNQ se obchoduje jen dopoledne: MNQ trades only in the morning
MNQ kopíruje cenu NQ, jen bod stojí 2 US: MNQ copies the NQ price, only a point costs 2 USD instead of 20 USD.
Draw on liquidity: kam cena nejspíš míří: Draw on liquidity: where price is most likely heading
Poslední dvě lekce jsme hledali likvidit: In the last two lessons we looked for liquidity and learned to tell a sweep from a breakout. Today one question ties it together: which liquidity will price go to next?
Té úrovni ICT říká draw on liquidity, zk: ICT calls that level the draw on liquidity, DOL for short. It is the target the market is most likely pulled towards, and it gives you two things at once: direction and a place to take profit.
Kandidáty už znáš: high a low předchozíh: You already know the candidates: the previous day's high and low, the overnight high and low, equal highs and equal lows. Buyside liquidity (BSL) sits above price, sellside liquidity (SSL) below it.
Který z nich je DOL? Podívej se, co cena: Which one is the DOL? Look at what price did last. If it has just taken the liquidity below and come back, the next target is usually on the other side, the BSL above.
Pomáhá i vzdálenost a zjevnost. Bližší a: Distance and how obvious a level is also help. A closer, clearer level, such as clean equal highs, is a more likely target than a distant high from last week.
DOL není signál ke vstupu. Říká jen, kam: The DOL is not an entry signal. It only tells you where to look. You look for an entry later, in a pullback towards the target and by your own rules.
Když cena začne dělat opak, například ni: If price starts doing the opposite, for example making lower lows instead of higher ones, your DOL no longer holds. Reassess it or leave the trade alone.
Ráno v 9:30 newyorského času je NQ na 21: At 9:30 New York time NQ is at 21,080. Below it is the overnight low at 21,010, above it yesterday's high at 21,190. At 9:41 price drops to 20,996, takes the overnight low and the candle closes back above it. The sellside liquidity below is taken, so the DOL is now yesterday's high at 21,190. You don't buy right away. You wait for the first pullback after the return above 21,010 and take profit just below 21,190.
Draw on liquidity je likvidita, ke které: The draw on liquidity is the liquidity price will most likely go to next. It gives direction and a target, but it is not an entry signal. After a sweep on one side, look for the DOL on the other.
Co je draw on liquidity?: What is the draw on liquidity?
Likvidita, ke které cena nejspíš půjde p: The liquidity price will most likely go to next
První svíčka po otevření trhu: The first candle after the market opens
DOL je cíl, ke kterému trh nejspíš táhne: The DOL is the target the market is most likely pulled towards. It gives direction and a target.
Cena právě vybrala noční low a zavřela z: Price has just taken the overnight low and closed back above it. Where should you most likely look for the DOL?
Ještě níž pod nočním low: Even lower, below the overnight low
Nahoře u buyside likvidity, třeba u včer: Above, at buyside liquidity, such as yesterday's high
Nikde, po sweepu se neobchoduje: Nowhere, you don't trade after a sweep
Sellside likvidita dole je vybraná. Dalš: The sellside liquidity below is taken. The next target is usually on the other side.
Víš, že DOL je nahoře. Kdy nakupuješ?: You know the DOL is above. When do you buy?
Hned, protože víš, kam cena jde: Right away, because you know where price is going
Až v korekci ve směru k cíli a podle svý: In a pullback towards the target and by your own rules
Až když cena DOL vybere: Only once price takes the DOL
The DOL tells you direction and target, not the moment to enter.
Displacement: pohyb, který ukáže, kdo má: Displacement: the move that shows who is in control
NQ v 9:44 newyorského času vybere noční: At 9:44 New York time NQ takes the overnight low at 21,010 and comes back above it. Until then the five-minute candles had a range of about 12 points. The next three candles go up, each covers 30 to 40 points from open to close and the wicks are only a few points. A quarter of an hour later price is at 21,115. That is displacement. You do not buy at 21,115. You mark the gap the move left between the first and third candle and wait to see whether price returns into it.
Displacement je rychlý pohyb jedním směr: Displacement is a fast one-way move made of large candles with small wicks. It shows that one side took control of the market. You do not jump into it, you wait for a return into the gap it left.
Minulý týden jsme hledali likviditu a cí: Last week we looked for liquidity and the target price is heading to. This week we look at how price sets off toward it. We start with the term displacement.
Displacement je rychlý pohyb jedním směr: Displacement is a fast move in one direction. It is made of several large candles in a row with big bodies and only small wicks.
Velké tělo znamená, že cena od otevření: A big body means price travelled a long way between the candle's open and close. A small wick means the other side barely pushed it back. So one side fully controlled the market for a moment.
V ICT je displacement důkaz, že za pohyb: In ICT, displacement is evidence that real interest stands behind the move, not just noise. That is why you wait for it after a sweep: the sweep shows where liquidity was taken, displacement shows that price really turned.
Jak ho poznáš od běžného pohybu? Porovne: How do you tell it from an ordinary move? Compare the candles with the ones before them. In displacement they are clearly larger than those around them and go one way without hesitation.
Do samotného displacementu se nenaskakuj: You do not jump into the displacement itself. By the time you see it, price is already far away and the stop would have to be wide. You wait for a return into the gap the move left behind. That gap is called a fair value gap and it is tomorrow's lesson.
Když se cena vrátí celým pohybem zpátky: When price comes all the way back to where the move started, the strength was only apparent. Do not treat such a move as displacement.
Velká těla a malé knoty ukazují, že jedn: Big bodies and small wicks show that one side took control of the market.
Několik velkých svíček jedním směrem s m: Several large candles in one direction with small wicks
Střídání rostoucích a klesajících svíček: Rising and falling candles taking turns
Vidíš tři velké svíčky nahoru. Co uděláš: You see three large candles up. What do you do?
Do displacementu se nenaskakuje. Vstup s: You do not jump into displacement. The entry is looked for in the return.
Hned koupím, dokud to jede: Buy right away while it is running
Počkám na návrat do mezery, kterou pohyb: Wait for a return into the gap the move left
Prodám, protože cena je moc vysoko: Sell because price is too high
Cena se po silném pohybu vrátila celou c: After a strong move price came all the way back to the start. What does that mean?
Skutečný displacement cenu posune a ta s: Real displacement moves price and it does not come all the way back.
Síla byla jen zdánlivá a pohyb jako disp: The strength was only apparent and I do not treat the move as displacement
Fair value gap: mezera, kterou za sebou: Fair value gap: the gap a fast move leaves behind
Včera jsme skončili u toho, že se do dis: Yesterday we ended with the point that you do not jump into displacement and you wait for a return into the gap. Today we look at that gap up close. It is called a fair value gap, FVG for short.
FVG tvoří tři svíčky jdoucí po sobě. Pro: An FVG is made of three candles in a row. The middle one is large, and price moves so fast in it that the wick of the first candle and the wick of the third never meet. An empty band is left between them.
Při růstu leží mezera mezi high první sv: In a rise the gap lies between the high of the first candle and the low of the third. In a fall it is the other way round, between the low of the first candle and the high of the third. The body of the middle candle passes through that band, but the first and third candles do not reach into it.
Proč na tom záleží? V tom pásmu se obcho: Why does it matter? In that band trading went almost only one way. In a rise, buyers took everything that was for sale and the other side could not react in time. ICT calls this an imbalance and expects price to return to such a place.
Jak mezeru najdeš: vezmi tři svíčky po s: How to find a gap: take three candles in a row and look only at the first and the third. If their wicks overlap, there is no gap, however big the middle candle is. If they do not overlap, mark the band between them with a rectangle.
Mezera sama není důvod k obchodu. Vzniká: A gap alone is not a reason to trade. Many of them form and not every one gets filled; in a strong trend price often leaves without coming back. The one that matters formed after a sweep during displacement, where structure changed. How to enter it and when it stops being valid is the topic of tomorrow's lesson.
NQ po výběru nočního low 21 010 vystřelí: After taking the overnight low at 21,010, NQ shoots up in three five-minute candles. The first has a high of 21,048. The second is large and closes at 21,090. The third has a low of 21,071. The first candle's wick ends at 21,048 and the third candle's wick starts only at 21,071, so they do not meet. Between 21,048 and 21,071 there is a fair value gap 23 points high. You mark it with a rectangle and wait to see whether price returns into it.
FVG je mezera mezi knotem první a třetí: An FVG is the gap between the wicks of the first and third candles, left by a large middle candle. Look for it after a sweep and displacement. On its own it is not a signal.
Které svíčky určují hranice FVG?: Which candles set the edges of an FVG?
Mezera leží mezi knotem první a knotem t: The gap lies between the wick of the first candle and the wick of the third. The middle one only passes through it.
Trh roste. První svíčka má high 21 048,: The market is rising. The first candle has a high of 21,048, the third has a low of 21,040. Is there an FVG?
Low třetí svíčky je pod high první. Knot: The low of the third candle is below the high of the first. The wicks met and no gap was left.
Ano, ale jen poloviční: Yes, but only half of one
Která mezera má největší váhu?: Which gap carries the most weight?
Mezer vzniká hodně. Smysl má ta, která v: Many gaps form. The one that matters formed where structure changed.
Každá, kterou na grafu najdeš: Every one you find on the chart
Ta, která vznikla po sweepu při displace: The one that formed after a sweep during displacement
Jak se FVG obchoduje: návrat, polovina m: How an FVG is traded: the return, the middle of the gap and when it stops holding
Včera jsme si ukázali, jak fair value ga: Yesterday we showed how to find a fair value gap. Today, how to work with it. In short: after displacement you wait for price to come back into the gap and enter in the direction of the original move.
Proč čekat na návrat? Když naskočíš do r: Why wait for the return? If you jump into a running candle, you buy high and the stop has to be far away. If you wait for the return into the gap, you buy cheaper and you know exactly where you are wrong.
Uprostřed mezery leží úroveň, které ICT: In the middle of the gap is a level ICT calls consequent encroachment, CE for short. It is halfway between the top and bottom edge. A strong gap often holds at its top edge or around CE. That is why the entry is often a limit order placed right in the gap or at CE.
Stop patří za začátek pohybu, tedy pod s: The stop goes beyond the start of the move, below the swing low displacement launched from. For a long after a sweep it is below the low price took. If the market goes there, the original idea is wrong.
Kdy mezera selhala? Knot přes CE ještě n: When has the gap failed? A wick through CE cancels nothing yet. A body closing below CE is a warning. It is fully invalid when price passes through the whole gap and a body closes beyond its far edge. Then it turns into something else, which we will cover with the inverse FVG.
A ještě jedna věc: ne každá mezera se vy: One more thing: not every gap gets filled and not every one is traded. If price leaves without coming back, there simply was no trade. You do not chase a missed move.
Navážeme na včerejší příklad. Na NQ je f: We build on yesterday's example. On NQ there is a fair value gap between 21,048 and 21,071, and CE is at 21,059.5. The swing low the move launched from is 21,010. You place a limit buy at 21,059.5 and a stop at 21,004, below the swing low. The risk is 55.5 points; on one MNQ contract at 2 dollars a point that is 111 dollars. Price comes back, wicks down to 21,052 and closes above CE. The gap holds. If a candle body had closed below 21,048, the idea would be gone and you would wait for a new setup.
Do FVG se vstupuje po návratu ceny, ve s: An FVG is entered after price returns, in the direction of the displacement. The middle of the gap is CE. A body below the whole gap means it failed.
CE je úroveň v půlce mezi horní a dolní: CE is the level halfway between the top and bottom edge of the FVG.
Horní hrana mezery: The top edge of the gap
Knot prostřední svíčky: The wick of the middle candle
Kam patří stop u longu z býčího FVG po s: Where does the stop go on a long from a bullish FVG after a sweep?
Když cena půjde pod začátek pohybu, půvo: If price goes below the start of the move, the original idea is wrong.
Pod swing low, ze kterého pohyb vyrazil: Below the swing low the move launched from
Nad horní hranu mezery: Above the top edge of the gap
Kdy býčí FVG úplně selhal?: When has a bullish FVG fully failed?
Knot nic neruší. Zavření těla za celou m: A wick cancels nothing. A body closing beyond the whole gap means it did not hold. If price never comes back, there simply was no trade.
Když tělo svíčky zavře pod celou mezerou: When a candle body closes below the whole gap
Když se cena do mezery vůbec nevrátí: When price never comes back into the gap
Inverzní FVG: když proražená mezera změn: Inverse FVG: when a broken gap switches sides
Včera jsme skončili tím, že mezera, za j: Yesterday we ended by saying that a gap a candle body closes beyond turns into something else. Today we finish that thought. ICT calls it an inversion fair value gap, or inverse FVG.
Princip je jednoduchý. Býčí mezera měla: The principle is simple. A bullish gap was supposed to hold price from below. When price passes through it and a body closes below its bottom edge, the gap has failed. On the next return from below, though, it often works the other way: as a ceiling. Support has become resistance. For a bearish gap the mirror applies.
Rozhoduje zavření těla, ne knot. Knot př: The body close decides, not the wick. A wick through the whole gap is just a spike. The inversion appears only when a candle body closes beyond the far edge. Until then it is still the original gap, just under pressure.
Proč to funguje? Kdo v mezeře kupoval, t: Why does it work? Those who bought in the gap are now at a loss. When price comes back to it, some of them are glad to get out at break-even, and that pushes price down. It is not a law, just a common pattern.
Vstup se hledá při návratu do inverzní m: The entry is looked for on the return into the inverted gap, most often around its middle, CE. The stop goes beyond the far edge of the gap. If a body closes back above it, the inversion is invalid and the trade is over.
Nejvíc váhy má inverze, která vznikne sp: An inversion that forms together with a structure break, for example at an MSS after a sweep, carries the most weight. An inversion in the middle of consolidation, where price goes back and forth, means little.
Pokračujeme ve včerejším příkladu. Býčí: We continue yesterday's example. The bullish FVG on NQ between 21,048 and 21,071 did not hold: a candle body closed at 21,039, below the whole gap. The gap is now inverted, and you wait to see whether it holds from above. Price drops to 21,015 and then comes back up. You place a limit short at CE 21,059.5 and a stop at 21,078, above the top edge. The risk is 18.5 points; on one MNQ at 2 dollars a point that is 37 dollars. If a candle body closed above 21,071, the inversion would be invalid and the trade gone.
Mezera proražená zavřením těla mění roli: A gap broken by a body close switches roles: support becomes resistance and vice versa. Entry around CE, stop beyond the far edge, valid only until a body closes back through the gap.
Kdy vzniká inverzní FVG z býčí mezery?: When does an inverse FVG form from a bullish gap?
The body close beyond the far edge decides. A wick is just a spike.
Když knot projde pod mezeru: When a wick goes below the gap
Když tělo svíčky zavře pod spodní hranou: When a candle body closes below the bottom edge of the gap
Jak se z býčí mezery po inverzi obvykle: How does price usually behave at a bullish gap after inversion when it returns from below?
Proražená mezera mění roli. Z podpory se: A broken gap switches roles. Support becomes resistance.
Mezera dál funguje jako podpora: The gap still acts as support
Mezera už nic neznamená: The gap no longer means anything
Kdy short z inverzního FVG přestává plat: When does a short from an inverse FVG stop being valid?
Zavření těla zpět přes mezeru inverzi ru: A body close back through the gap cancels the inversion. A wick above CE does not yet.
Když cena klesne k dalšímu low: When price drops to the next low
Když knot sáhne nad CE: When a wick reaches above CE
Když tělo svíčky zavře zpátky nad mezero: When a candle body closes back above the gap
